Package com.egradx.notification.repository

Interface EgradxNotificationDeliveryRepository

All Superinterfaces:
org.springframework.data.repository.CrudRepository<EgradxNotificationDeliveryEntity,UUID>, org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.JpaRepository<EgradxNotificationDeliveryEntity,UUID>, org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.JpaSpecificationExecutor<EgradxNotificationDeliveryEntity>, org.springframework.data.repository.ListCrudRepository<EgradxNotificationDeliveryEntity,UUID>, org.springframework.data.repository.ListPagingAndSortingRepository<EgradxNotificationDeliveryEntity,UUID>, org.springframework.data.repository.PagingAndSortingRepository<EgradxNotificationDeliveryEntity,UUID>, org.springframework.data.repository.query.QueryByExampleExecutor<EgradxNotificationDeliveryEntity>, org.springframework.data.repository.Repository<EgradxNotificationDeliveryEntity,UUID>
public interface EgradxNotificationDeliveryRepository extends org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.JpaRepository<EgradxNotificationDeliveryEntity,UUID>, org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.JpaSpecificationExecutor<EgradxNotificationDeliveryEntity>
The result-recording updates below are all guarded on attempts = :attempts AND status = PENDING. That guard is what makes a lapsed lease safe: if a dispatcher took so long that its lease expired and another instance re-claimed the row (incrementing attempts), the slow dispatcher's result matches nothing and is discarded rather than overwriting the newer attempt.

  • Method Details

    • lockDueBatch

      @Query(value="SELECT * FROM egradx_notification_delivery WHERE status = \'PENDING\' AND next_attempt_at <= :now ORDER BY next_attempt_at LIMIT :batchSize FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED", nativeQuery=true) List<EgradxNotificationDeliveryEntity> lockDueBatch(@Param("now") Instant now, @Param("batchSize") int batchSize)
      The next batch of due deliveries, locked for the calling transaction. SKIP LOCKED lets any number of instances run a dispatcher at once: each takes whatever rows the others have not, and none waits on another. A native query because JPQL has no SKIP LOCKED.

      @Query(value="SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE next_attempt_at <= :now) AS due, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE next_attempt_at > :now) AS waiting FROM egradx_notification_delivery WHERE status = \'PENDING\'", nativeQuery=true) EgradxNotificationDeliveryRepository.Backlog countBacklog(@Param("now") Instant now)
